Hi Sara — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the private deployment decision (Private VPC / PrivateLink vs Dedicated):

What we heard from your side
- Primary requirement: isolate inference traffic inside your AWS accounts, strict outbound allowlist, and no changes to existing cross-account routing policies if possible.
- Preference toward a model that minimizes routing changes and requires the smallest blast radius for network teams.

Redwood recommendation based on your constraints
- PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink) is usually the lower-friction option for teams that can accept endpoint services — it avoids cross-account peering and route table changes.
- VPC peering is viable if your security team prefers direct VPC routes; it requires CIDR planning and route table updates.
- Dedicated capacity (Redwood Dedicated) remains an alternative if you want predictable throughput without integrating into your VPC, but it won't meet your isolation requirement unless combined with our Private customer networking options.

Info we need from CloudOps to produce a concrete provisioning plan
1) L3 network diagram (simple VPC, subnets, NATs, IGW, firewall) — attach if available.
2) AWS Account IDs and VPC IDs you want to connect to.
3) CIDR blocks for the target VPCs and any transit VPCs.
4) Which option you prefer for inbound connectivity: PrivateLink (recommended) or VPC Peering.
5) Allowlist requirements — do you need a fixed set of Redwood egress IPs, or can you accept a PrivateLink endpoint?
6) Maintenance windows / change freeze windows and an escalation contact for network approvals.

Deliverables from Redwood after we get the above
- A short runbook showing steps for both PrivateLink and VPC peering (what your team must do, what Redwood does).
- A stub security group/ACL template and example route entries.
- Timeline and cost delta between Hosted/Dedicated/Private options for your expected QPS.

Can you share the L3 diagram and preferred account/vpc ids by end-of-day Thursday? If that works, I will prepare the runbook and loop in Rishi (SE) and Grace (Solutions) to schedule a 30-minute technical handoff next week.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks — quick technical note and action items from the SE side.

Short tech notes:
- PrivateLink path: customer creates interface endpoint(s) in each AZ/subnet you want traffic to originate from and accepts the Redwood endpoint service. No route table changes required; inbound goes over AWS-managed ENIs. We will provide the service name and an acceptance ARN.
- VPC peering path: requires non-overlapping CIDRs and route table updates in each peered VPC. Latency is slightly lower for peering but operational burden is higher for multi-account setups.
- Egress IPs: we can provide a short-lived list of egress IPs for firewall allowlisting; for longer-term stable traffic we recommend PrivateLink. If you need fixed IPs, we can propose a NAT + egress IP pool in a dedicated account (adds time/cost).

Proposed checklist for Tuesday tech session:
1) Confirm which subnets will host interface endpoints (PrivateLink) and for which AZs.
2) Confirm a single acceptance owner who can accept the endpoint service in the account console (we'll provide step-by-step).
3) Validate SG rules: allow TCP 443 from your app subnets to the endpoint ENIs; drop other inbound.
4) If peering is chosen, validate non-overlapping CIDR ranges and provide the route table who will own updates.

Deliverables I'll bring to the call:
- PrivateLink acceptance template (one-click copy instructions).
- Example SG/ACL fragments and a short connectivity test plan.
- Preliminary egress IP list (if Acme asks).

Action items (owners/dates):
